newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India issues term tender to buy 0.25-pct diesel.
newsitem.headline: India issues term tender to buy 0.25-pct diesel.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a one-year term tender to buy 0.25-percent sulphur diesel for May 1997-April 1998 deliveries, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Kandla, on the west coast, traders said on MOnday.
The tender seeks one 40,000-to-45,000-tonne cargo of 0.25-percent diesel per month. It closes on March 13 and offers will be valid until March 17.
This is the first time that IOC has issued a one-year term tender to buy the 0.25-percent diesel grade.

IOC has already issued two other annual term tenders to buy 1.0-and-0.5-percent sulphur diesel as well as superior kerosene for May 1997-April 1998 deliveries, both of which closes on March 13 sa well.
India started importing about 60,000-tonne spot cargoes of 0.25-percent sulphur diesel a month since the middle of 1996.

IOC requires this lower sulphur diesel to prepare the country for a gradual switch from the 1.0-and-0.5-percent sulphur grade by April 1999 to curb air pollution due to a rise in diesel-driven vehicles.
